How many won games have you lost on time? 👇

ig_caption:
Winning on the board, losing on the clock? Time is part of the position.

Five habits that help: remember that a flag still loses; spend your minutes on the moves that change the game, not on recaptures; play with increment; premove only the truly forced moves; and when you're ahead and short of time, trade pieces and keep it simple.

How many won games have you lost on time? 👇

#chess #chessimprovement #chesstips #blitz #rapidchess #learnchess #chessjourney
alt: Slide 1: Cover. Winning, then flagged? Five clock habits. Time is a piece too.
Slide 2: Habit 1. Running out of time loses, however far ahead you are, unless your opponent cannot possibly mate.
Slide 3: Habit 2. Spend seconds on obvious recaptures and minutes on moves that change the position.
Slide 4: Habit 3. Play with increment, such as 10+5 instead of 10+0, so endgames aren't a race.
Slide 5: Habit 4. Premove only forced recaptures, never when your opponent has a choice.
Slide 6: Habit 5. Ahead but low on time? Trade pieces so there is less to calculate.
Slide 7: A Chess Journey poster. Every flag is on the graph, and so is every save.

slides.title: A flag still loses
slides.body: Run out of time and you lose, however far ahead you are. The only exception: if your opponent cannot possibly checkmate, it's a draw.
slides.note: A won position only counts once you finish it.

slides.title: Spend time where it matters
slides.body: An obvious recapture needs seconds. A move that changes the position, a new threat, a trade, a pawn break, deserves minutes.
slides.note: Ask: is this position different from the last one?

slides.title: Play with increment
slides.body: Increment adds a few seconds after every move, so a long endgame no longer turns into a race against the clock.
slides.note: Try 10+5 instead of 10+0 for a week.

slides.title: Premove only the forced
slides.body: A premove saves time but doesn't look at the board. Use it for forced recaptures, never when your opponent has a choice.

slides.title: Ahead? Trade pieces
slides.body: Up material with little time left? Swap pieces off. Fewer pieces means fewer threats to calculate, and quicker, safer moves.
slides.note: A simple win beats a brilliant flag.

slides.title: Every flag is on the graph.
slides.sub: Your whole rating history, on one print.
